builds.model:
Files are uot_sink.py (the model), check_solvers.py (unit checks), extra_paired.py, uot_sink_<dataset>.json/.log/_scores.npz and extra_paired.json. The run is STRICT rolling origin: transition i (snapshot i -> i+1) reads only snapshots 0..i.
(1) Archetypes. A Poisson/KL NMF of the pooled bin counts S_b = n_b*m_b over bins 0..i, so S ~ W H (H rows sum to 1, deterministic farthest-point init). K in {4,8,16} with K_eff = min(K, i), so there are always fewer states than bins.
(2) Cells. UMI per cell of each state is ell_k = 1/c_k, from a ridge fit of sum_k W_bk c_k = n_b (weights n/(n+50), shrunk to the pooled value, clipped to [1/4,4]x). Cell fractions are pi_bk proportional to W_bk c_k, and absolute masses are w_bk = n_b*pi_bk. The per-cell mean profile is A_k = H_k/c_k, so m_b ~ pi_b A. The nonzero-fraction profile F comes from a fixed-pi KL fit.
(3) Cost. C_kl = mean_g (log1p(1e4 H_k) - log1p(1e4 H_l))^2, divided by its mean off-diagonal value.
(4) Couplings for the last R in {1,3} past pairs (j-1 -> j), eps in {0.05, 0.2}:
- balanced: entropic OT on proportions with the existing hpc/sinkhorn.py (ablation without the sink).
- sink_abs (the task's formulation): an augmented balanced problem on ABSOLUTE masses. The source side is the K states plus a reservoir of mass N_dst; the target side is the K states plus a sink of mass N_src. Cost state->sink = reservoir->state = lambda (in {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1}), reservoir->sink = 0. The plan blocks are transport, death and birth, and deaths - births = N_src - N_dst holds exactly (unit-checked).
- sink_norm: the same augmentation on proportions (both totals equal to 1), which separates the sink from the sampling-driven cell counts.
- kluot_abs: KL-relaxed unbalanced Sinkhorn (Chizat), own log-domain iterations, f = -(tau*eps/(tau+eps)) LSE, tau in {0.1, 1, 10}.
(5) Rates. Per pair, the kernel is Q_k. = P_k./a_k (transport plus death) and births per source cell are beta = P_birth/N_src. These are pooled over the R pairs with weights omega_j*a_k. The push-forward is w_hat = w_i Q + N_i beta, and pi_hat = w_hat/sum (the forecast total is not scored). Other forecasters in the same pipeline: persist, lin1 (pi_i + (pi_i - pi_{i-1}), clipped), and the ORACLE (bin i+1 projected on the strict archetypes; NOT strict).
(6) Map back by mixture shift. m_hat = pi_hat A + rbar_L, where rbar_L is the residual m_b - pi_b A averaged over the last L in {1,3} bins. L=1 gives m_i + (pi_hat - pi_i) A; L=3 gives a denoised level. Targets:
- l1 = log1p(CP10k(m_hat)) - log1p(CP10k_i)
- linear = m_hat - m_i
- orig: a finite-cell head, p0 = (1 - f_hat)^n_i plugged into the clipped log-ratio.
(7) Selection. Within each reported group (family x K), rolling origin picks the config with the best mean (PCC + tie-aware P@K up + down)/3 over all genes, past transitions j in [max(1,i-8), i-1]. At i <= 1 the fallback is trend (persist + head for orig). There are 300 configs.
In practice the selected lambda is 0.1 almost everywhere. Turnover then costs 0.2, less than nearly every pairwise cost, so the chosen "sink OT" has almost no transport block: it is stay / die / be-born, i.e. multiplicative decline of shrinking states plus additive birth into growing ones.
Scores use dileo_rescore.metrics on 25% gene masks (rng = default_rng(1000*s + i), s in 0..2), averaged over transitions i >= 1 and then over seeds.

builds.interpretation:
(1) sink_abs (the absolute-count sink) does not measure cell death. deaths - births equals n_src - n_dst exactly. At lambda >= 0.5 the free turnover is about 0: on every pair either D=0 or B=0, e.g. pancreas 612->361 cells gives D=251, B=0. So that sink only tracks how many cells were sampled per bin, a property of the dataset design rather than biology. Using absolute counts also hurts l1 on both datasets.
(2) The readable part is sink_norm (equal totals). Turnover is 2-8 % of mass per pair at lambda=0.5 (0 at lambda=1), and it is uncorrelated with |d log n| (Spearman -0.14 to +0.01), so it is not a sampling artefact.
- Pancreas, K8: states that 'die' (death fraction per pair) are progenitor/ductal-like DDIT4L/VNN1/TK1 (0.28), SDS/DLL1/SOSTDC1 (0.22) and cycling CEP55/BUB1/CENPF (0.19). Mass is 'born' into NHLH1/NEUROD2 endocrine progenitors (30 % of births), ADRA2C/POU3F1/TFF3 (32 %), SST (13 %) and INS/GCG (12 %). This reads as proliferating progenitors leaving and endocrine states appearing.
- Gastrulation, K8: early bins are dominated by an erythroid state (HBE1/SLC4A1/HEMGN, 94 % of bin 2) and late bins by an endothelial state (CDH5/ESAM/HAPLN1, 87 % of the last bin). Deaths fall on erythroid states (HBZ/HBQ1/ALAD 0.27; HBE1/SLC4A1 0.25). Births go to SNRPN/PRSS50 (26 %), SPP1/GZMB (26 %), CDH5/ESAM (12 %) and RAB27B (12 %).
(3) For forecasting, the selected cheap sink (lambda 0.1) is just multiplicative decline plus additive birth. On l1/linear it equals balanced OT and lin1 within noise. On orig it helps because a softer turn-off of shrinking states feeds the zero-count head.
caveats: Primary target l1: the sink does not help. sink_abs loses to balanced on both datasets. sink_norm is +0.012 PCC on gastrulation (p=0.09; dJ p=0.0096) and -0.011 on pancreas. Neither beats the denoised-level baseline (persist L3) significantly.

beats_trend_l1 = False because it holds only on gastrulation (0.269 vs -0.158). On pancreas every composition model, the oracle ceiling included (0.164), is below trend (0.177), so this is structural, not tuning.

beats_their_corrected_best_l1 = True, with caveats. On gastrulation the whole margin comes from the denoised level: persist L3 alone scores 0.255 vs their 0.104, so it does not come from any coupling. On pancreas P@200-down is 0.209 < their 0.235. Their numbers were computed on their own masks.
n_b is the number of cells sampled per bin (dataset design), not a population size. That is why the absolute-mass sink mostly encodes |d n|.
The selected lambda is mostly 0.1. The winning 'sink OT' therefore has an essentially empty transport block (stay / die / be-born).

orig: sink_norm on pancreas (0.465) exceeds the oracle composition (0.44). This is an effect of the zero-count head (softer turn-offs), not composition skill. Our orig numbers remain below the quoted DistBridge orig (0.585 gastrulation, 0.488 pancreas; other masks).

On gastrulation l1 the oracle composition reaches 0.42 vs 0.27 for the forecasts. Composition matters, but it cannot be forecast from 1-3 past couplings. Composition TV improves only at the hindsight-best lambda.

K=16 is never reached on pancreas (K_eff <= 13) and only for i >= 16 on gastrulation, since K_eff = min(K, i). K4 is selected about 90 % of the time. Archetypes come from <= 30 bin-aggregate profiles only (no single cells).

builds.model:
Each gene is handled separately. Its per-bin cell-count law comes from dist_bridge: P(c=0)=1-f, and c|c>0 = 1+NB (or Poisson) matched to the positive-part mean mu and variance v. Bins t-L and t share a count-scale grid built as in dist_bridge.grid_masses. The one change: integer grids stop at K = the smallest of {2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,32,48} that is >= cmax, the 99.9% quantile (genes are bucketed by K). Genes with cmax>48 keep the 48-point linear grid. A bucketed balanced run reproduces dist_bridge.coupling+sb_step with corr 1.0000.

Transported measure: expressing mass per cell, a_j = f_A pA_j and b_l = f_B pB_l, so the totals f_A and f_B differ.

Sink/source problem (own solver uot_sinkhorn.solve_tv, batched over genes): min_T <T,C> + eps KL(T|R) + lam_g(f_A - |T|) + lam_g(f_B - |T|), subject to T1 <= a and T^T1 <= b.
- C_jl = (c_j - c_l)^2/2.
- Sink s = a - T1, destroyed at A's levels. Source beta = b - T^T1, created at B's levels.
- Reference R = min(f_A,f_B) (a/f_A) x (b/f_B), so entropy alone does not push mass into the sink.
- lam_g = lam0 * max(mu_B, (v_A+v_B)/2): a cell is sunk and re-created rather than moved once its count would change by more than about 2 sqrt(lam0) sd.
- eps_g = 0.25 L mu_B, the same as dist_bridge's count scale.
- Dual updates (one-sided TV aprox = clip): f = min(lam, eps[log(f_A/m0) - LSE_y(log b~_y + (g_y - C_xy)/eps)]), and g the same way. Plan T = m0 a~ b~ exp((f+g-C)/eps).
- eps-scaling from Cmax down to eps, plus a translation step (f+c, g-c) that puts the potential of the heavier side at lam.
- This is the eps->0 limit of the dummy-node problem (level->sink lam, source->level lam, source->sink 0). The explicit dummy-node version with plain Sinkhorn was tried first and dropped: it did not converge for lam >> eps, and at small lam its entropy pushed 20-40% of the mass through the dummies.

Forecast, delta bins ahead, at each level l of today's grid:
- Death probability over L bins is d_l = s_l/a_l. Survival (1-d_l)^(delta/L) is applied to all mass now at l.
- Only the transported part c_l = sum_j T_jl moves, by delta v_l with v_l = (z_l - barycentre of its origin)/L (v=0 where c_l < 1e-6 b_l).
- Born mass stays at z_l, and births continue: delta beta_l/L is added at z_l.
- Positions below 1/2 switch off. f_hat = surviving + born mass, capped at 1. The forecast triplet (m, f, E[c^2]) comes from these masses.
- Gene with f_A=0<f_B: f_B(1+delta/L) with the same positive law. f_B=0: forecast 0.

Targets:
- l1 = dist_bridge.expected_value of log1p(1e4 S/(n_t Lhat)) - log1p(CP10k_t), with n_t cells drawn from the forecast law (256 draws), today's library L_t and forecast library Lhat = sum m_hat.
- l1_plugin = plug-in log1p CP10k change.
- linear = m_hat - m_t.
- orig = dist_bridge.expected_target finite-cell head.

Grid: lam0 in {128,4,1,0.25,0.0625}, L in {1,3} (Le = min(L,i)), delta in {1,0.5,2}.

Strict rolling-origin selection per transition i, separately per target and family:
- Criterion: mean dist_bridge.criterion J (Pearson + tie-aware P@K up + down, all genes, K = 200 N/n_test) over past transitions max(1,i-8)..i-1, targets from bins <= i.
- Ties within 1e-3 go to the larger lam0.
- i=1 has no past transition and uses the a-priori default (lam0=1, L=1, delta=1); i=0 is never scored.

Families:
- uot: full grid, the model.
- uot_forced: lam0=128 only. Sink and source then carry only the forced |f_A-f_B|, so this is the same extrapolation rule without OT choosing levels.
- uot_lam<x>: one lam0 at a time (the lam0 profile).
- bal: no-sink ablation, i.e. DistBridge's transport step (OT between normalised positive parts plus a log-linear trend of f) on the same grid and solver, L x delta.
- persist: delta=0, today's law plus the same head.
- trend: repeat last change.

Scoring: dileo_rescore.metrics on masks np.random.default_rng(1000 s + i).permutation(G)[:n_test], s in {0,1,2}. Mean over transitions, then over seeds, for i>=1 and i>=2. Also an all-gene PCC that needs no mask, and a paired Wilcoxon over transitions.

Runtime on 14 processes: pancreas 5 min, gastrulation 18.5 min. Scripts: run_uot.py, uot_core.py, uot_sinkhorn.py, posthoc.py, level_check.py, mask_check.py.

builds.interpretation:
Measures are per-cell expressing fractions. The sink is therefore "cells that stop expressing or shrink relative to the population", and the source is the reverse.

When lam0 >= 4 (dying only if a count would move by more than about 4 sd), OT uses the sink and source for nothing beyond the forced change in nonzero fraction:
- Excess death is 0.000 to 0.0001.
- Pancreas: 8.8% of the expressing mass per bin at L=1 (15.6% at L=3).
- Gastrulation: 3.9% (4.3% at L=3).
- That loss is spread almost evenly over count levels: pancreas death 8.7% at count 1 vs 9.6% at counts >= 2; gastrulation 4.6% vs 3.4%. Dying cells carry 1.09-1.16x the gene's mean count.
- So at a fair price the data never need cells to switch off or appear selectively at particular count levels. The change in a gene's law between bins is explained by smooth shifts of the surviving cells.

When the sink is cheap (lam0 0.25 to 0.0625), OT chooses to turn over the UPPER tail:
- Gastrulation lam0=0.0625, L=1: 38% of the mass at counts >= 2 is sunk vs 11% at count 1, and births are the same (39% vs 11%).
- Pancreas: 44% vs 13%.
- Dying and newborn mass sits at 1.4-2x the gene's mean count.
- Read literally, the changes are carried by high-expressing cells (a subpopulation) leaving and arriving, not by every cell shifting.
- Extrapolated, this turnover predicts further loss for genes whose high-count tail was replaced. That is why the down side of the ranking improves on linear (both datasets) and on gastrulation l1 while the up side and PCC fall.
- Part of this is a level rule: the lam0=0.0625 linear forecast correlates with -m_t at r=0.36-0.37, against 0.04-0.09 for lam0=128, bal and trend; on gastrulation l1 it is 0.19 vs 0.02. Not pure persistence (corr with persist ~0).
- At this cheap price the sink works as a high-expression decline prior. It does not identify which cells die.

The extrapolation rule (per-level death hazard plus continuing births), tested on its own as uot_forced vs bal, loses to the log-linear nonzero-fraction trend on l1 PCC on both datasets (p=0.03).

Total sink mass vs log(n_t/n_{t-L}) is not a usable signal: r = +0.24 to +0.55 on gastrulation L=1 and about -0.3 on pancreas L=3, with only 11-27 points. This fits the global cell-number change dividing out of per-cell targets.
caveats: sink_helps is false on both datasets: uot loses to the balanced ablation on l1 PCC (pancreas -0.031, p=0.001; gastrulation -0.015, p=0.08) and to its own forced-only control (lam0=128). The lam0 profile is monotone: more sink means worse PCC and worse P@up. Even the non-strict hindsight-best UOT config is below the hindsight-best balanced config on both datasets.

beats_trend_l1 is false. Gastrulation yes (+0.141, 24/4), but the gastrulation trend is negative (-0.158), so that is not evidence. Pancreas no (-0.024, 5/8, p=0.41). beats_their_corrected_best_l1 is false: pancreas yes (0.153 vs 0.094), gastrulation no (-0.017 vs 0.104).

The balanced ablation is DistBridge's transport step on RAW bins with delta > 0 only: no box/Kalman pools and no delta=0 in its grid. That is why it scores -0.002 on gastrulation l1, where the CONTEXT DistBridge (pooled, delta=0 allowed) scores 0.137. Comparisons inside the script are paired and valid. The CONTEXT DistBridge / NASS / theirs rows are unpaired and on unknown masks.

On gastrulation l1 the best row is persistence plus the observation head (delta=0): 0.012/0.139/0.168. uot vs persist is 14/14 (p=0.60). The transport step adds nothing there, with or without a sink. On orig, OT costs about 0.03-0.09 PCC against persistence on both datasets.

Mask sensitivity (mask_check.py): across draw conventions the trend l1 PCC moves from -0.158 to -0.177 (gastrulation) and 0.144 to 0.177 (pancreas), and linear moves by about 0.1. P@200 moves by only about 0.003. My mask draw (permutation[:n_test], seeds 1000s+i) gives a pancreas trend l1 PCC of 0.177 against the CONTEXT 0.159. The all-gene PCC is the stable comparator: the gastrulation trend gives -0.169, exactly the CONTEXT value.

Solver: the first attempt (explicit dummy sink/source nodes with plain or eps-scaled Sinkhorn) did not converge for lam >> eps, and at small lam its entropy leaked 20-40% of the mass through the dummies. It was replaced by one-sided TV-penalised entropic UOT with eps-scaling and a translation step. A few genes per coupling still miss tol within 1500 final sweeps: max potential move 0.33 eps, max marginal overshoot 0.016 absolute mass, balanced max row error 0.008. lam0=4 and lam0=128 give practically identical diagnostics and scores, so the effect is negligible, but this is 'nearly converged', not converged.

The grid differs from dist_bridge: integer grids stop at the smallest bucket >= the 99.9% quantile instead of always 48 levels, done for speed. This was checked against dist_bridge on 600 genes (corr 1.0000, small max diff).

The masses are per-cell expressing fractions f*p, not absolute cell counts. The global change in n_t divides out because the targets are per-cell means. A version with absolute cell-count masses, which would need an n_{t+1} forecast, was not run, so 'cells that die' here means relative loss.

The lam0 selection sits on the lower grid boundary for linear: pancreas picked 0.0625 in 11 of 12 transitions, and gastrulation picked low lam0 in 12 of 27. The grid was not extended downward, because as lam0 -> 0 the model degenerates to re-sourcing all mass, a level-proportional or persistence-like rule. On l1 the selection mostly picks lam0=128 or 4, inside the grid.

The i>=1 averages include i=1, which runs on the a-priori default config (lam0=1, L=1, delta=1). i>=2 rows are given as well. Observation-head Monte Carlo draws are deterministic, keyed by (dataset, kind, i, L, lam0, delta, target).
Sink mass vs log cell-number ratio changes sign between datasets and lags (11-27 points), so it should not be interpreted.

_node_*.npz caches are regenerable)","C:\\Users\\Gabriele\\My Drive\\PhD & Research\\Temporal GNN\\tack\\results\\signal_analysis\\uot_judge\\p2 (rerun copy and outputs; pickles in the scratchpad folder judge_p2 are regenerable)","C:\\Users\\Gabriele\\My Drive\\PhD & Research\\Temporal GNN\\tack\\results\\signal_analysis\\uot_judge\\_trunc_pancreas-human_8 (truncation test outputs, regenerable)"],"verdict_plain":"Cosa abbiamo provato: due modi di aggiungere al trasporto ottimale (OT) un 'pozzo' e una 'sorgente', cioè un posto dove le cellule possono sparire o comparire tra un intervallo e il successivo. Il primo lavora sulla popolazione: riassume ogni intervallo in pochi tipi di cellule e sposta le loro quote. Il secondo lavora gene per gene, guardando quante cellule esprimono il gene e a che livello. Perché contava: il numero di cellule per intervallo cambia moltissimo (da 7 a 982), quindi un OT che deve conservare tutta la massa sembrava sbagliato in partenza. Come ho controllato: ho rifatto girare da zero tutti e due gli script e i risultati sono identici al numero. Ho rimescolato a caso i dati futuri e le previsioni non cambiano, quindi nessuno guarda il futuro. Ho ricalcolato con codice mio dati, maschere e punteggi, e ho confrontato ogni modello con la sua versione senza pozzo sugli stessi geni. Risultato: il pozzo non rende utile l'OT. Sul target principale (l1) non batte in modo affidabile la versione senza pozzo. Il piccolo vantaggio sulla gastrulazione (+0.01) sparisce se si confrontano configurazioni uguali, ed è riprodotto da una regola di una riga senza nessun trasporto: i tipi che calano continuano a calare in proporzione, quelli che crescono aggiungono l'ultimo aumento. Sul pancreas stanno tutti sotto al semplice 'ripeti l'ultimo cambiamento', anche l'oracolo che conosce la composizione vera. Il modello per gene con il pozzo perde contro il suo controllo senza pozzo su tutti e due i dataset. Sul target lineare il pozzo non aiuta: o peggiora, o guadagna sui geni in discesa e perde su quelli in salita. Contro NASS, il nostro migliore, perde in ogni transizione del pancreas e in 20 su 27 della gastrulazione. Batte DistBridge e il loro modello migliore solo sulla gastrulazione, ma lì ci riesce anche la semplice media degli ultimi 3 intervalli, senza OT; sul pancreas le differenze stanno dentro il rumore dovuto alla scelta dei geni di test. Cosa sono le masse del pozzo: con i conteggi assoluti sono solo quante cellule sono state campionate in ogni intervallo, una scelta di chi ha fatto il dataset e non biologia. Con le proporzioni sono un rimescolamento della composizione: nel pancreas escono i progenitori in divisione ed entrano le cellule endocrine, nella gastrulazione escono le cellule del sangue. È una descrizione dei cambi di proporzione, non morte cellulare misurata. Per gene, a prezzo giusto il pozzo porta solo il calo della frazione di cellule che esprimono il gene; a prezzo basso diventa la regola 'i geni molto espressi caleranno'. Perché non funziona: con 15-30 istantanee medie e nessuna cellula seguita nel tempo, il pozzo non ha informazione nuova. Quello che può imparare c'è già nella tendenza recente o nel livello medio, e i parametri in più aggiungono solo rumore nella scelta della configurazione. Unica nota positiva: la versione 'rilassata' (KL) batte l'OT bilanciato sulla gastrulazione, ma non batte la semplice media dei livelli recenti."}
